note: Literature in English round 3 (part B): genre and forms, themes and characterisation, plot/setting/structure and narrative techniques - each item built around a scenario or mini-extract - plus general items on the widely read set texts (Antony and Cleopatra, To Kill a Mockingbird, An Inspector Calls, A Man for All Seasons, The Marriage of Anansewa, The Lion and the Jewel, Second Class Citizen, Wuthering Heights, So the Path Does Not Die) and the commonly prescribed African and non-African poems.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A play in which a proud general destroys himself and those he loves through his own jealousy, ending in several deaths, is best classified as
questions.explanation: A serious play ending in the downfall of a great figure through a flaw is a tragedy.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A play full of mistaken identities, slamming doors and absurd coincidences, written purely to make the audience laugh, is
questions.explanation: Farce relies on exaggerated situations, physical humour and improbable plots.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A play in which the innocent heroine is tied to a railway line by a moustache-twirling villain and rescued at the last moment by a flawless hero is
questions.explanation: Melodrama features sensational plots, stock characters of pure good and evil, and strong appeals to emotion.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A play that begins with a shipwreck and threats of death but ends with forgiveness, reunion and a wedding is
questions.explanation: A tragicomedy mixes serious danger with a happy ending, as in Shakespeare's late romances.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A short play with a single act, one setting and a story that takes about forty minutes to perform is
questions.explanation: A one-act play is a complete drama in a single act, usually with few characters and one situation.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A dramatic work in which the whole story is told through the songs of the actors, with no spoken dialogue, is
questions.explanation: Opera is drama set entirely to music and sung.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A performer tells a whole story through bodily movement and facial expression without using any words. This form is
questions.explanation: Mime conveys action and emotion through gesture alone.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A prose fiction of about eighty pages, longer than a short story but shorter than a novel, is
questions.explanation: A novella is a mid-length prose narrative, such as 'Animal Farm' or 'The Old Man and the Sea'.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A prose narrative that can be read at one sitting, with few characters and a single main incident, is
questions.explanation: The short story concentrates on one effect or incident and a small cast.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A story such as 'The Tortoise and the Birds', in which animals act like humans and a moral is drawn, is
questions.explanation: A fable is a brief tale, often with animal characters, that teaches a moral.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A traditional story that explains how the sky came to be far from the earth is
questions.explanation: Myths are traditional stories that explain natural phenomena, origins or beliefs.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A traditional story about Moremi of Ile-Ife, a historical figure whose deeds have been embellished over generations, is
questions.explanation: Legends are traditional stories about human heroes believed to have lived, often mixing fact and exaggeration.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A short story told to illustrate a moral or spiritual lesson, such as the story of the Prodigal Son, is
questions.explanation: A parable is a simple story used to teach a moral or religious truth.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A novel in which the villain is a cruel factory owner and the plot exposes child labour in order to press for reform is best described as
questions.explanation: A social-problem (thesis) novel dramatises a social evil to argue for change, as Dickens often did.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A novel that follows a roguish hero of low birth through a series of loosely connected adventures on the road is
questions.explanation: The picaresque novel is episodic and centres on a resourceful rogue (picaro).

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A novel set in a gloomy castle with secret passages, ghosts, a persecuted heroine and a sinister villain belongs to the
questions.explanation: Gothic fiction features mystery, terror, decaying settings and the supernatural.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A novel set during the Nigerian Civil War that includes real generals and real battles alongside invented characters is
questions.explanation: Historical novels place fictional characters within real past events.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A prose narrative in which a clever hare repeatedly outwits stronger animals, told by an elder to children, belongs to
questions.B: the epistolary tradition of the novel
questions.C: the sonnet tradition of lyric poetry
questions.D: the trickster tale tradition of oral literature
questions.explanation: Trickster tales (Tortoise, Hare, Ananse) are a staple of African oral literature.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A poem of praise chanted for a Yoruba king, listing his ancestors, attributes and deeds, is an example of
questions.explanation: Oriki and similar forms are oral praise poems addressed to persons, lineages or towns.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A short poem expressing the personal feelings of a single speaker, often musical in quality, is
questions.explanation: Lyric poetry expresses the thoughts and emotions of a speaker; it was originally sung to the lyre.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A poem in which a duke, speaking to a visitor, unintentionally reveals that he had his last wife killed, is
questions.explanation: In a dramatic monologue a single speaker addresses a silent listener and reveals his character, as in Browning's 'My Last Duchess'.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A poem that idealises the simple life of shepherds in the countryside is
questions.explanation: Pastoral poetry presents rural life, especially that of shepherds, in an idealised way.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A poem that uses the grand style of the epic to describe a trivial quarrel over a stolen lock of hair is
questions.explanation: The mock epic applies heroic conventions to trivial subjects for comic effect, as in Pope's 'The Rape of the Lock'.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A sonnet that divides into an octave rhyming abbaabba and a sestet rhyming cdecde is
questions.explanation: The Petrarchan sonnet has an octave and a sestet with a turn (volta) between them.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The change in thought or mood between the octave and the sestet of a sonnet is called the
questions.explanation: The volta or 'turn' marks the shift in argument in a sonnet.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A short poem ending with a witty or surprising twist, such as 'I am His Highness' dog at Kew; / Pray tell me, sir, whose dog are you?' is
questions.explanation: An epigram is a brief, pointed poem or saying, often ending in a sting.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A poem inscribed on a tombstone or written as if for one, summing up the life of the dead person, is
questions.explanation: An epitaph commemorates the dead; an epigraph is a quotation at the start of a work.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A quotation placed at the beginning of a novel or chapter to suggest its theme is
questions.explanation: An epigraph is a motto or quotation prefixed to a work or section.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A speech or section added at the end of a play or novel to round off the story is
questions.explanation: An epilogue concludes a work; a prologue introduces it.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A long poem such as 'Sundiata' or 'The Iliad' celebrating the deeds of a national hero in elevated language is
questions.explanation: The epic is a long narrative poem on a grand scale about heroic deeds.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A poem that laments the death of a friend and ends with consolation is
questions.explanation: The elegy is a poem of mourning, usually moving from grief towards consolation.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: Free verse differs from blank verse in that free verse
questions.A: is written only in couplets, while blank verse uses quatrains
questions.B: always rhymes, while blank verse never does
questions.C: has neither regular metre nor rhyme, while blank verse is unrhymed iambic pentameter
questions.D: is used only in drama, while blank verse is used only in lyrics
questions.explanation: Blank verse keeps a regular metre (iambic pentameter) without rhyme; free verse abandons regular metre too.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A novel that presents a nightmarish future society controlled by a totalitarian government is
questions.explanation: Dystopian fiction imagines an oppressive future world, as in Orwell's '1984'.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: An account of the writer's own life, such as Wole Soyinka's 'Ake: The Years of Childhood', is
questions.explanation: An autobiography is a life story written by its subject; a biography is written by someone else.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A play that presents the everyday problems of ordinary people in a realistic setting, using natural dialogue, is called
questions.explanation: Realistic (domestic) drama depicts ordinary life credibly, as in Ibsen's plays.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In the theatre, the group of performers who comment on the action and sing between scenes, as in Greek tragedy, is the
questions.explanation: The chorus in Greek drama comments on events and expresses communal views.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A literary work in which every character and event stands for an abstract idea, such as Bunyan's 'The Pilgrim's Progress', is
questions.explanation: Allegory carries a second, symbolic level of meaning throughout.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In a novel, a young woman defies her father, her village and her church to marry a man of a different tribe, and the story follows the consequences. The central theme is
questions.B: the corrupting influence of political power
questions.C: the conflict between individual choice and communal tradition
questions.explanation: The heroine's personal choice is set against the demands of family, community and religion.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A play shows a headmaster who preaches honesty at assembly but sells examination papers at night. The play's main concern is
questions.explanation: The gap between what the character professes and what he does is the essence of hypocrisy.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A novel set in a Lagos slum follows a family that loses its home to a demolition ordered to make way for a luxury estate. The dominant theme is
questions.B: social injustice and the plight of the poor
questions.explanation: The poor are dispossessed for the benefit of the rich, which foregrounds injustice.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A character who is described only as 'the greedy landlord' and behaves exactly the same on every appearance is
questions.explanation: Flat characters are built around a single trait and do not develop.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A heroine who is generous yet vain, brave yet impulsive, and who surprises the reader by her decisions is
questions.explanation: Round characters are complex, many-sided and capable of surprising the reader convincingly.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In a play the hero's timid, cautious friend is placed beside him so that the hero's recklessness stands out. The friend serves as
questions.explanation: A foil is a character whose qualities contrast with and highlight those of another.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A character who begins a novel as a selfish miser and ends it as a generous benefactor after a night of visions is
questions.explanation: A dynamic character undergoes significant inner change, like Scrooge in 'A Christmas Carol'.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: Throughout a long novel the loyal servant remains exactly as faithful and cheerful at the end as at the beginning. He is
questions.explanation: A static character does not change in the course of the work.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The main character of a novel is a cowardly, dishonest clerk with no admirable qualities, yet the story centres on him. He is
questions.explanation: An anti-hero is a central character who lacks conventional heroic virtues.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A character to whom the heroine confides her secrets so that the audience learns her thoughts is
questions.explanation: The confidant exists largely to receive the protagonist's confidences.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In a play, the villain's greed, ambition and hypocrisy are revealed not by the author's comment but through his own speeches and actions. This method of characterisation is
questions.explanation: Indirect characterisation lets readers infer traits from speech, action and the responses of others.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A novelist writes, 'Chief Odili was a mean, suspicious man who trusted nobody.' This is an example of
questions.explanation: The narrator states the character's traits explicitly.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A hero who is noble and admired but whose downfall is caused by excessive pride is a
questions.explanation: The tragic hero, in Aristotle's sense, is a great person brought down by a flaw (hamartia), often pride (hubris).

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In a novel about the civil war, the constant presence of vultures over every scene of fighting is a
questions.explanation: A motif is a recurring image or element that reinforces a theme.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A play repeatedly shows fathers ruining their sons through excessive ambition for them. The recurring idea is the play's
questions.explanation: The theme is the central idea explored through the action.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In a story, a man who reported his neighbour to the secret police is himself arrested on the same neighbour's false report. This outcome illustrates
questions.explanation: Poetic justice is the fitting reward of virtue or punishment of vice within the work.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A novel about a village girl who goes to the city, is corrupted by easy money and returns home broken deals mainly with the theme of
questions.D: the destructive lure of urban life
questions.explanation: The city's temptations and their cost form the central concern.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A poem describes a soldier's return to a village that no longer recognises him. Its central concern is
questions.explanation: The returning soldier's estrangement from his own community is alienation.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A play presents a ruler who silences journalists, rigs elections and jails his rivals, and the chorus laments the people's suffering. The play is chiefly concerned with
questions.B: the conflict between love and duty
questions.C: political oppression and the abuse of power
questions.explanation: Tyranny and its effects on the people dominate the action.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A character called 'the Common Man' who plays a steward, a boatman, a jailer and an executioner in the same play represents
questions.A: the supernatural forces controlling the plot
questions.B: a single historical figure of great importance
questions.C: the playwright himself appearing on stage
questions.D: the ordinary person who adapts to survive under any regime
questions.explanation: In Bolt's 'A Man for All Seasons' the Common Man stands for ordinary, self-preserving humanity.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In a novel, the heroine's wicked stepmother, her handsome prince and her fairy godmother are all instantly recognisable types. Such characters are
questions.explanation: Stock characters are conventional types familiar from many stories.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A novelist shows a corrupt minister being kind to his children and generous to beggars while stealing public money. The purpose is most likely to
questions.A: show that the minister is a static character who never changes
questions.B: prove to the reader that corruption does no real harm to anyone
questions.C: present a complex, believable character rather than a simple villain
questions.D: make the reader admire the minister and excuse his corruption
questions.explanation: Mixing virtues and vices makes a round, credible character.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A play in which a mother sacrifices her savings, health and reputation to see her son through university, only to be abandoned by him, explores the theme of
questions.B: war and its aftermath in a village
questions.explanation: The mother's sacrifice and the son's ingratitude form the central idea.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: Two brothers in a novel take opposite paths: one stays to farm the family land, the other goes abroad and forgets home. The novelist uses them to explore
questions.B: the tension between tradition and modernity
questions.explanation: The contrasting brothers embody the pull between old ways and new.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The character through whose eyes and sympathies the reader experiences most of a novel is the
questions.explanation: The protagonist is the central figure whose fortunes the reader follows.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In a play, the villain is not a person but the drought that slowly destroys the village. The antagonist here is
questions.explanation: The antagonist may be a person, society, nature or the hero's own weakness.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A poem in which a market woman's cheerful bargaining hides her grief for a dead child presents the character mainly through
questions.A: direct statement of her qualities by the poet
questions.B: contrast between outward behaviour and inner feeling
questions.C: the opinions expressed by the other market women
questions.D: detailed physical description of her appearance
questions.explanation: The gap between appearance and inner reality reveals her character.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A novel about a lawyer who defends an innocent man against a hostile town, knowing he will lose, explores chiefly
questions.C: moral courage in the face of prejudice
questions.explanation: Standing for justice despite certain defeat is moral courage, as in Atticus Finch.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A play about a girl promised in marriage to four suitors by her scheming father explores mainly
questions.A: the loneliness of exile in a foreign country
questions.B: the horrors of civil war and the plight of refugees
questions.C: religious conversion and the clash of faiths
questions.D: greed, cunning and the commodification of marriage
questions.explanation: The father's trading of his daughter for gifts is the mainspring of 'The Marriage of Anansewa'.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A play in which a whole wealthy family is shown to share responsibility for a poor girl's suicide is chiefly concerned with
questions.explanation: Priestley's 'An Inspector Calls' insists that 'we are responsible for each other'.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A poem in which a father tells his son that people now 'laugh with their teeth' and 'shake hands without hearts' deals with the theme of
questions.A: patriotic sacrifice in the struggle for freedom
questions.B: the beauty of nature and the changing seasons
questions.C: hypocrisy and the loss of sincerity in modern life
questions.D: the joy of friendship between children at play
questions.explanation: Okara's 'Once Upon a Time' laments the false manners of modern society.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A poem in which the speaker ignores the arrest of his neighbours one after another until the soldiers come for him deals with
questions.A: the wonder of creation and the natural world
questions.B: the pleasures of village life and farming
questions.C: the sorrow of lost love and separation
questions.D: indifference to injustice and its consequences
questions.explanation: Osundare's 'Not My Business' shows that silence in the face of tyranny finally costs the silent.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A novel opens with the hero already on trial for murder and then goes back to narrate the events that led to the crime. The opening technique is called
questions.explanation: Beginning 'in the middle of things' plunges the reader into the action before the background is supplied.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The part of a play in which the characters, setting and situation are introduced is the
questions.explanation: Exposition provides the background information needed to follow the plot.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The event that sets the main conflict of a story in motion, such as the arrival of a stranger claiming the hero's land, is the
questions.explanation: The inciting incident launches the central conflict.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The series of events in which tension mounts as the hero struggles against obstacles is the
questions.explanation: Rising action builds complications towards the climax.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The moment in a tragedy when the hero discovers that the man he has killed was his own father is
questions.explanation: The climax is the point of highest tension and decisive change in the hero's fortunes.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The events that follow the climax and lead towards the ending are the
questions.explanation: Falling action shows the consequences of the climax.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The French term for the final unravelling of the plot, in which mysteries are explained and the fate of characters settled, is the
questions.explanation: Denouement means 'untying' - the resolution of the complications.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A novel begins with the hero as an old man, then moves back to his childhood, and the rest of the book works forward to the opening scene. This structure uses
questions.explanation: Flashback (analepsis) narrates events earlier than the story's present.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In the first chapter a fortune-teller warns that 'water will take what fire has spared'. In the last chapter the hero drowns. The early warning is an example of
questions.explanation: Foreshadowing hints at events to come.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In a play about a king's fall, the comic quarrels of two servants run alongside the main action. The servants' story is
questions.explanation: A subplot is a secondary line of action that parallels or contrasts with the main plot.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A novel set in Enugu in 1967, in a house where every window has been taped against bomb blasts, uses setting mainly to
questions.B: describe the beauty of the landscape
questions.C: establish the atmosphere and historical context of war
questions.explanation: Time and place here root the story in the Nigerian Civil War and create tension.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The time, place and social circumstances in which the action of a work occurs are together called the
questions.explanation: Setting includes historical period, geographical location and social environment.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A story in which the whole action takes place in one room during a single night observes
questions.explanation: The classical unities restrict a play to one place, one day and one action.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A novel in which each chapter is narrated by a different member of the same family, all describing the same funeral, has
questions.explanation: Several narrators giving their own versions of events create a multiple-perspective structure.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A play in which the conflict is resolved by the sudden arrival of a rich uncle nobody had mentioned uses a device called
questions.explanation: Deus ex machina is an improbable, contrived resolution introduced from outside the plot.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A novel is told as a sequence of loosely connected episodes on a journey, any of which could be removed without damaging the story. Its plot is
questions.explanation: Episodic plots string together separate incidents, as in picaresque fiction.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A story ends where it began, with the hero once again waiting at the same bus stop, so that the reader feels nothing has changed. The structure is
questions.explanation: A circular (cyclical) structure returns to the opening situation.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The struggle between the hero and the forces opposing him, which drives the plot forward, is called
questions.explanation: Conflict is the clash of opposing forces at the centre of plot.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A character who must choose between saving his brother and keeping a promise to his dying father faces
questions.explanation: The struggle within a character's own mind is internal (man versus self) conflict.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A novel in which a fisherman battles a giant marlin and then sharks for three days presents mainly
questions.explanation: The struggle against natural forces is external conflict of the man-versus-nature kind.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A novel about a whistle-blower persecuted by his ministry, his neighbours and the press presents mainly
questions.D: conflict between the individual and society
questions.explanation: The hero's struggle is against social institutions and pressures.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A short story in which a woman waits by a phone for news of her son, and the story ends without the call coming, uses
questions.explanation: An open ending leaves the outcome unresolved for the reader to imagine.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A play in which the final scene shows the lovers married, the villain jailed and every mystery explained has
questions.explanation: A closed ending ties up all the threads of the plot.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: When a novel of many chapters is called 'well-made', the praise refers mainly to
questions.B: the beauty of its landscape descriptions
questions.D: the tight, logical arrangement of its plot
questions.explanation: A well-made plot is carefully constructed so that every incident contributes to the whole.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A play in five acts in which the hero's fortunes rise until the third act and decline thereafter follows
questions.explanation: Freytag's pyramid places the climax at the centre with rising action before and falling action after.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A novelist interrupts a tense scene of a robbery to spend a chapter on the hero's childhood. The interruption is
questions.A: the denouement, where all mysteries are explained
questions.B: the climax of the novel, where tension is highest
questions.C: a digression or flashback that delays the main action
questions.D: an example of comic relief after a tense scene
questions.explanation: A move away from the main action into earlier events is a flashback or digression.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In a novel the physical setting - a decaying mansion whose walls crack as the family quarrels - functions chiefly as
questions.A: a subplot running beside the main plot
questions.D: a symbol of the family's collapse
questions.explanation: Setting can mirror and symbolise the state of the characters.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The statement 'The king died and then the queen died of grief' differs from 'The king died and then the queen died' in that the first
questions.A: is a setting, because it names the place
questions.B: is a plot, because it supplies causality
questions.C: is a theme, because it states an idea
questions.D: is a subplot, because it is secondary
questions.explanation: E. M. Forster's distinction: a story is events in time; a plot is events linked by cause.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A novel set 'in a town very much like Onitsha, in the years just after independence' has a setting that is
questions.explanation: The setting draws on a real place and period without naming them exactly.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A tense, comic scene of a drunken porter joking at the gate immediately after a murder is an example of
questions.explanation: Comic relief eases tension in a serious work, as with the Porter in 'Macbeth'.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In a play, the last speech announces that the young couple will rebuild the burnt village together. This constitutes the
questions.explanation: The resolution settles the outcome of the conflict.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Narrative Techniques and Point of View
questions.q: 'I was nine the year the soldiers came, and I remember the smell of the burning market more than anything.' The point of view is
questions.explanation: The narrator uses 'I' and tells his own experience.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Narrative Techniques and Point of View
questions.q: 'Amaka did not know that her brother, two streets away, was at that moment signing the papers that would ruin them both.' The narrator is
questions.explanation: The narrator knows what Amaka does not and what is happening elsewhere - an all-knowing point of view.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Narrative Techniques and Point of View
questions.q: 'She watched the door. Whatever he was deciding on the other side, she could only guess.' The narration is
questions.A: first person told by the woman herself
questions.B: third person limited to one character
questions.explanation: The narrator uses 'she' but is confined to her knowledge and perceptions.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Narrative Techniques and Point of View
questions.q: 'You wake before the alarm. You dress in the dark so as not to wake her. You do not yet know this is the last time.' The narration is in the
questions.explanation: The narrator addresses the character as 'you'.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Narrative Techniques and Point of View
questions.q: A story is narrated by a proud swindler who insists that everyone he cheated deserved it. The reader is expected to see more than he admits. He is
questions.explanation: An unreliable narrator's account cannot be taken at face value because of bias, ignorance or self-deception.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Narrative Techniques and Point of View
questions.q: A narrator reports only what could be seen and heard, like a camera, never entering any character's mind. This is
questions.explanation: The objective narrator records externals only, as in Hemingway's 'Hills Like White Elephants'.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Narrative Techniques and Point of View
questions.q: A novel is told by the hero's friend, who observes and reports the hero's rise and fall. This is
questions.explanation: The narrator is a minor participant who tells someone else's story, like Nick in 'The Great Gatsby'.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Narrative Techniques and Point of View
questions.q: A novel consists entirely of letters exchanged between two sisters, one in Lagos and one in London. The technique is
questions.explanation: The epistolary novel tells its story through letters (or diaries, e-mails).

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Narrative Techniques and Point of View
questions.q: 'Rain again - Mama's cough - the bus fare - if only - forty naira short - his shoes, oh his shoes -' This passage uses
questions.explanation: The unpunctuated flow of associated thoughts imitates the mind at work.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Narrative Techniques and Point of View
questions.q: A tale in which an old sailor tells his story to a wedding guest, so that the main story is enclosed inside another, uses
questions.explanation: A frame narrative is a story within a story, as in Coleridge's 'Rime of the Ancient Mariner'.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Narrative Techniques and Point of View
questions.q: 'Dear reader, you may well ask why she did not simply leave him. I shall tell you.' This is an example of
questions.explanation: The narrator steps out of the story to address the reader directly.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Narrative Techniques and Point of View
questions.q: A chapter presents the same accident first through the driver's eyes and then through the victim's. The technique is
questions.B: shifting or multiple point of view
questions.explanation: The narrative perspective moves between characters.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Narrative Techniques and Point of View
questions.q: Instead of writing 'She was angry', the novelist writes, 'She set the plate down so hard the rice jumped.' This illustrates the technique of
questions.explanation: Showing presents concrete action for the reader to interpret; telling states the feeling.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Narrative Techniques and Point of View
questions.q: 'Ten years passed. The children grew, the roof was mended twice, and Papa's hair turned white.' This is an example of
questions.explanation: Summary compresses a long period into a few sentences, unlike a scene presented moment by moment.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Narrative Techniques and Point of View
questions.q: A play uses a Storyteller who speaks directly to the audience, introduces characters and comments on their behaviour. This device draws on
questions.explanation: Sutherland's 'The Marriage of Anansewa' adapts the Ananse storyteller into the play.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Narrative Techniques and Point of View
questions.q: 'He said he would come. He said it twice. He said it the way he said everything - as if saying it made it so.' The narrator's attitude is conveyed chiefly through
questions.explanation: The dry repetition and comment reveal the narrator's sceptical tone.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Narrative Techniques and Point of View
questions.q: A novel about a war is narrated by a child who reports the adults' quarrels without understanding them, so the reader grasps more than the narrator. This creates
questions.explanation: The gap between the naive narrator's understanding and the reader's produces irony.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Narrative Techniques and Point of View
questions.q: In a novel the reader is told what every character in the village thinks, but the narrator never judges them. The narrator is best described as
questions.explanation: The narrator has full knowledge but withholds comment.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Narrative Techniques and Point of View
questions.q: A novelist tells a story of a marriage entirely through the husband's diary. A disadvantage of this technique is that
questions.A: the story cannot have a plot
questions.B: the reader learns the thoughts of every character
questions.C: the reader knows only what the diarist chooses to record
questions.D: the wife's feelings are reported directly
questions.explanation: A single subjective document limits and possibly distorts what the reader can know.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Narrative Techniques and Point of View
questions.q: 'The story you are about to read was found in a tin box in my late uncle's room. I have changed nothing.' This opening device is intended to
questions.explanation: The 'found manuscript' frame makes the fiction seem like a real document.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Narrative Techniques and Point of View
questions.q: In a play, a character alone on stage says, 'Now I am alone. O, what a rogue and peasant slave am I!' The speech is
questions.explanation: A soliloquy is a speech in which a character alone reveals inner thoughts.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Narrative Techniques and Point of View
questions.q: In a play, while two characters talk, a third turns to the audience and mutters, 'He lies; I saw him take it.' This is
questions.explanation: An aside is a brief remark heard by the audience but not by the other characters.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Narrative Techniques and Point of View
questions.q: In drama, information about the past - a murder ten years ago, a lost will - is conveyed through the dialogue of characters rather than by a narrator. This is called
questions.explanation: Plays deliver background information through what characters say and do.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Narrative Techniques and Point of View
questions.q: Notes in a play such as '(She crosses to the window, her back to him)' are
questions.explanation: Stage directions instruct actors and directors on movement, gesture and setting.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Narrative Techniques and Point of View
questions.q: A novelist reproduces the speech of a Warri trader exactly as it sounds - 'Na wetin dey happen?' The use of such speech is called
questions.explanation: Dialect gives characters authenticity and local flavour.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Narrative Techniques and Point of View
questions.q: An author who writes 'The little thief was, as thieves go, a rather charming one' is using
questions.explanation: The narrator's wry judgement colours the description.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Narrative Techniques and Point of View
questions.q: A short story ends with a sudden reversal - the beggar the heroine has been feeding turns out to be her long-lost father. The device is
questions.explanation: A twist ending overturns the reader's expectations at the close, as in O. Henry's stories.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Narrative Techniques and Point of View
questions.q: The novelist presents a whole scene through what a servant overhears from behind a door. The servant is functioning as
questions.explanation: A focaliser is the character through whose perception the scene is filtered.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Narrative Techniques and Point of View
questions.q: A novel written entirely in the present tense - 'She opens the door. The room is empty.' - creates mainly
questions.B: a sense of distance from events long past
questions.D: immediacy, as if events unfold before the reader
questions.explanation: Present-tense narration makes action feel immediate.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Narrative Techniques and Point of View
questions.q: In an oral tale the narrator pauses to ask the listeners, 'And what do you think the tortoise did next?' before continuing. This shows that oral narrative is
questions.explanation: Oral performance involves audience participation and response.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In 'The Marriage of Anansewa', Ananse collects gifts from four chiefs by promising each of them his daughter. To escape the trap he has set for himself, he
questions.A: marries Anansewa to the first chief who paid
questions.C: stages Anansewa's death to test which chief truly loves her
questions.D: confesses everything to the chiefs and returns their gifts
questions.explanation: The mock funeral reveals that only Chief-Who-Is-Chief responds with genuine love and generosity.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The Storyteller in 'The Marriage of Anansewa' functions mainly to
questions.A: represent the colonial government and its officers in their dealings with the village
questions.B: act as Ananse's chief rival for the gifts sent by the four chiefs to Anansewa
questions.C: play the part of the fourth chief in disguise so that Anansewa will not recognise him
questions.D: narrate, comment on the action and link the play to the Ananse folktale tradition
questions.explanation: Sutherland's 'Anansegoro' form adapts the oral storyteller into the theatre.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The musical interludes in 'The Marriage of Anansewa', performed by the players and audience, are called
questions.explanation: The mboguo are songs that comment on and advance the action, drawn from the Akan storytelling tradition.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In 'The Marriage of Anansewa', Anansewa finally marries
questions.explanation: Chief-Who-Is-Chief proves his love by his response to the news of her 'death', and she 'revives' to marry him.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: Ananse in 'The Marriage of Anansewa' is best described as
questions.A: a colonial officer imposing new laws
questions.B: a noble chief betrayed by his daughter
questions.C: a foolish servant who cannot understand money
questions.D: a cunning trickster whose schemes nearly destroy him
questions.explanation: Ananse, the spider of folklore, is the archetypal trickster.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In 'The Lion and the Jewel', Sidi rejects Lakunle's proposal chiefly because he
questions.A: is much older than she is and already has grey hair
questions.B: refuses to pay the bride price, which she sees as an insult
questions.C: is already married to two wives in another village
questions.D: has no education and cannot read the magazine
questions.explanation: Lakunle calls the bride price a 'savage custom'; Sidi thinks refusing it would brand her as no virgin.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: Baroka in 'The Lion and the Jewel' wins Sidi by
questions.A: threatening to banish her family from Ilujinle if she refuses to become his wife
questions.B: paying a far larger bride price than Lakunle could ever afford to pay for her
questions.C: pretending to Sadiku that he has become impotent, so that Sidi comes to mock him
questions.D: promising to send her to school in Lagos and to build her a house with a tin roof
questions.explanation: Sadiku spreads the false news; Sidi visits Baroka to taunt him and is seduced.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In 'The Lion and the Jewel', Lakunle's half-digested Western ideas and his scorn for village customs make him
questions.B: the tragic hero of the play
questions.C: the wise voice of the community
questions.D: a comic figure whose modernity is shallow
questions.explanation: Soyinka satirises Lakunle's confused, imitative 'progress'.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The title 'The Lion and the Jewel' refers to
questions.explanation: Baroka, the Bale, is the lion; Sidi, the village belle whose photograph appears in a magazine, is the jewel.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A feature that distinguishes much African drama from the European well-made play is
questions.A: the use of a single set and a single scene throughout the whole performance
questions.B: the total absence of any conflict between the characters from beginning to end
questions.C: the integration of song, dance, drumming and audience participation into the action
questions.D: the complete exclusion of comic elements from plays on serious subjects
questions.explanation: African drama typically draws on communal performance traditions.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In 'The Marriage of Anansewa', Christie (Christiana Yamoah) is
questions.B: one of the four chiefs who court Anansewa
questions.C: Anansewa's grandmother who opposes the marriage
questions.D: Ananse's helper and companion who assists his schemes
questions.explanation: Christie supports Ananse in managing the chiefs and the mock funeral.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In 'The Lion and the Jewel', the mime of the stranger with the camera, performed by the villagers, is an example of
questions.A: a soliloquy spoken by Lakunle to the audience
questions.B: a play within the play used to narrate past events
questions.C: an aside addressed to Sadiku by Baroka
questions.D: an epilogue that closes the action of the play
questions.explanation: The villagers act out the photographer's earlier visit - drama used as flashback.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In 'Antony and Cleopatra', Antony marries Octavia in order to
questions.A: obey the command of the Roman Senate
questions.C: strengthen his political alliance with Octavius Caesar
questions.explanation: The marriage to Caesar's sister is a political bond that Antony soon breaks by returning to Egypt.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: Enobarbus in 'Antony and Cleopatra' deserts Antony but dies soon afterwards because
questions.A: he is fatally wounded at the battle of Actium while covering Antony's retreat
questions.B: Caesar has him executed as a traitor who cannot be trusted by either side
questions.C: Cleopatra poisons him for advising Antony to fight on land instead of at sea
questions.D: he is overwhelmed by shame when Antony sends his treasure after him
questions.explanation: Antony's generosity breaks Enobarbus's heart: 'I fight against thee! No: I will go seek some ditch wherein to die.'

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The famous description of Cleopatra on her barge - 'The barge she sat in, like a burnished throne, / Burned on the water' - is spoken by
questions.explanation: Enobarbus describes her first meeting with Antony at Cydnus in Act 2.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: At the battle of Actium, Antony loses because he
questions.A: is betrayed by Octavia, who sends his plans to Caesar
questions.B: refuses to fight at sea although his generals urge him to
questions.C: follows Cleopatra's fleeing ships and abandons the fight
questions.D: is wounded by Caesar in single combat before the battle
questions.explanation: Antony flies 'like a doting mallard' after Cleopatra's ships.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: Antony tries to kill himself after receiving false news that
questions.explanation: Cleopatra sends Mardian to say she has died; Antony falls on his sword but does not die at once.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: Cleopatra chooses to die by the bite of the asp mainly because she
questions.A: wishes to be reunited with Julius Caesar
questions.B: refuses to be led in triumph through Rome by Caesar
questions.C: has been condemned to death by the Egyptian priests
questions.D: wants to punish Charmian and Iras
questions.explanation: She will not be shown to 'the shouting varletry of censuring Rome' or mocked on the stage.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: 'Age cannot wither her, nor custom stale / Her infinite variety' is said of
questions.explanation: Enobarbus sums up Cleopatra's endless fascination.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The central conflict in 'Antony and Cleopatra' is between
questions.B: Cleopatra and Octavia over a throne
questions.C: Caesar and Pompey over the corn supply
questions.D: Antony's Roman duty and his passion for Cleopatra
questions.explanation: Rome (duty, discipline, politics) is set against Egypt (pleasure, love, excess).

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In 'An Inspector Calls', Eva Smith lost her job at Birling's factory because she
questions.B: led a group of workers asking for higher wages
questions.C: was rude to a customer in the shop
questions.explanation: Birling sacked her for asking for a rise after the strike.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In 'An Inspector Calls', Sheila's part in Eva Smith's downfall was that she
questions.A: kept her as a mistress and then abandoned her
questions.B: refused her charity at the Brumley Women's Organisation
questions.C: had her dismissed from Milwards out of jealousy and bad temper
questions.D: got her pregnant and stole money to support her
questions.explanation: Sheila used her family's influence to have the shop girl sacked.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: Mrs Birling's contribution to Eva Smith's fate in 'An Inspector Calls' was that she
questions.A: arranged for her to be sent away so that Gerald would forget her
questions.B: sacked her from the family factory for asking for higher wages
questions.C: reported her to the police for stealing money from the shop
questions.D: used her influence to refuse the girl help from a charity committee
questions.explanation: Mrs Birling turned the pregnant girl away, blaming the unknown father - who was her own son Eric.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: Mr Birling's confident claims in 'An Inspector Calls' that the Titanic is 'unsinkable' and that there will be no war are examples of
questions.A: foreshadowing of a happy ending for the Birling family
questions.B: dramatic irony, since the 1945 audience knows he is wrong
questions.C: comic relief provided by a foolish servant character
questions.D: poetic justice, since his predictions come true
questions.explanation: The play is set in 1912, and the audience knows what followed.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The Inspector's final speech in 'An Inspector Calls' warns that if men do not learn responsibility for one another they will be taught it 'in fire and blood and anguish'. The speech expresses the play's
questions.A: romantic subplot between Sheila and Gerald
questions.D: Gothic atmosphere of terror and mystery
questions.explanation: Priestley's socialist message is delivered through the Inspector.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: At the end of 'An Inspector Calls', the telephone rings to announce that
questions.A: Birling has received the knighthood he was hoping for
questions.B: Gerald has been arrested for his part in the girl's death
questions.C: Eric has run away from home and taken the stolen money
questions.D: a girl has just died and a police inspector is on his way
questions.explanation: After the family decides Goole was a hoax, the real call restores the mystery and the moral.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In 'An Inspector Calls', the characters who show genuine remorse are
questions.explanation: The younger generation accepts responsibility; the parents care only about scandal.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In 'A Man for All Seasons', Sir Thomas More refuses to
questions.B: attend the King's wedding to Catherine of Aragon
questions.C: swear the oath acknowledging the King as head of the Church in England
questions.D: allow his daughter Margaret to marry
questions.explanation: More's conscience will not let him take the oath under the Act of Supremacy.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In 'A Man for All Seasons', Richard Rich secures More's conviction by
questions.B: producing a letter More wrote to the Pope
questions.explanation: Rich falsely swears that More denied the King's title; More notes he has sold his soul 'for Wales'.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In 'A Man for All Seasons', More's legal defence rests on the principle that
questions.A: the King is above the law and therefore cannot be a party to a trial
questions.B: silence must be taken as consent, so his silence cannot be treason
questions.C: a Lord Chancellor cannot be tried by any court below Parliament
questions.D: conscience is a matter for Parliament and not for individual men
questions.explanation: More argues 'qui tacet consentire' - the law presumes that silence gives consent, not denial.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: When Roper says he would cut down every law in England to get at the Devil, More replies that he would give the Devil benefit of law
questions.A: because Roper is a lawyer and must respect the courts
questions.B: because the Devil is innocent until he is proved guilty
questions.C: for his own safety's sake, because laws protect everyone
questions.D: because the King commands it and must be obeyed
questions.explanation: 'When the last law was down, and the Devil turned round on you - where would you hide?'

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The Common Man in 'A Man for All Seasons' addresses the audience directly and changes roles on stage. This technique is associated with
questions.A: melodrama and its stock heroes and villains
questions.B: classical Greek tragedy and the use of a chorus
questions.C: the well-made play of the nineteenth century
questions.D: epic theatre and the breaking of dramatic illusion
questions.explanation: Bolt borrowed Brechtian devices to keep the audience thinking rather than merely feeling.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In Pede Hollist's 'So the Path Does Not Die', Fina's life is shaped by
questions.A: the death of her parents in the civil war
questions.B: an initiation ceremony that was left incomplete in her childhood
questions.C: her marriage to a wealthy chief in Freetown
questions.D: her election as a village leader
questions.explanation: Her father's intervention in the Bondo initiation leads to the family's exile and Fina's lasting sense of not belonging.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: 'So the Path Does Not Die' moves between Sierra Leone and
questions.explanation: Fina leaves Freetown for America, where she faces the problems of immigrant life.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A central concern of 'So the Path Does Not Die' is
questions.A: the rivalry between two football clubs and the violence between their supporters
questions.B: the struggle for independence from colonial rule and the rise of the first nationalists
questions.C: the corruption of a military government and the journalists who try to expose it
questions.D: the harm done by female genital mutilation and the search for identity in the diaspora
questions.explanation: The novel examines a harmful tradition, women's choices and the alienation of the immigrant.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In 'Second Class Citizen', Francis burns the manuscript of Adah's first novel, 'The Bride Price'. This act shows him as
questions.A: jealous and determined to crush her independence
questions.B: a supportive husband who wanted a better draft
questions.C: a publisher who rejected her work
questions.D: a religious man opposed to fiction
questions.explanation: The burning of the manuscript is the final blow that leads Adah to leave him.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The title 'Second Class Citizen' refers to Adah's status
questions.A: as a black immigrant woman in London and as a woman in her own culture
questions.B: as a junior civil servant in the Lagos office of the American consulate
questions.C: as a student who failed her examinations and lost her scholarship
questions.D: as the second wife of Francis, who married another woman in London
questions.explanation: Adah is doubly marginalised - by race in England and by gender at home.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In 'Unexpected Joy at Dawn', the separated siblings Nii Tackie and Mama Orojo live in
questions.explanation: The novel is set against the expulsions of aliens between Ghana and Nigeria.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A common feature of African novels such as 'Things Fall Apart' and 'So the Path Does Not Die' is
questions.A: the tension between traditional customs and modern or foreign values
questions.B: the use of the epistolary form of letters throughout the whole novel
questions.C: a setting entirely in Europe with no scenes on the African continent
questions.D: the absence of any female characters of importance to the plot
questions.explanation: Culture conflict is a major theme in African fiction.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: Adah in 'Second Class Citizen' can best be described as
questions.A: determined and resilient in the face of repeated setbacks
questions.B: timid and completely dependent on Francis
questions.explanation: Adah fights for education, work and independence against her husband and society.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In 'To Kill a Mockingbird', the story is narrated by
questions.A: Scout (Jean Louise Finch), looking back on her childhood
questions.B: Atticus Finch, recalling the trial many years later
questions.C: Jem Finch, writing as a lawyer in his old age
questions.D: an omniscient narrator who enters every character's mind
questions.explanation: The adult Scout recalls events in Maycomb when she was a child.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In 'To Kill a Mockingbird', Atticus Finch defends
questions.A: Tom Robinson, a black man accused of raping Mayella Ewell
questions.B: Boo Radley, accused of murdering Bob Ewell
questions.C: Bob Ewell, accused of assaulting the children
questions.D: Dill, accused of running away from home
questions.explanation: The trial of Tom Robinson is the centre of the novel.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: Atticus tells his children it is 'a sin to kill a mockingbird' because mockingbirds
questions.A: do nothing but sing and harm no one
questions.C: are the rarest birds in Alabama
questions.explanation: The mockingbird symbolises innocents such as Tom Robinson and Boo Radley.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In 'To Kill a Mockingbird', Boo Radley finally emerges to
questions.A: save Jem and Scout from Bob Ewell's attack
questions.C: confront Atticus about the children's games
questions.explanation: Boo kills Bob Ewell while protecting the children; Sheriff Tate says Ewell 'fell on his knife'.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: Atticus's advice that you never understand a person 'until you climb into his skin and walk around in it' expresses the novel's theme of
questions.explanation: Learning to see from another's point of view is central to Scout's growth.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: Scout disperses the lynch mob outside the jail by
questions.A: talking innocently to Mr Cunningham about his son and his legal troubles
questions.B: threatening the men with the shotgun that Atticus keeps in the house
questions.C: calling the sheriff on the telephone from the newspaper office
questions.D: singing a hymn with Calpurnia until the men become ashamed
questions.explanation: Her childish courtesy shames Cunningham into leading the men away.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: Mrs Dubose in 'To Kill a Mockingbird' is used by Atticus to teach Jem that real courage is
questions.A: fighting on when you know you are licked before you begin
questions.B: a man with a gun in his hand facing down a dangerous enemy
questions.C: never speaking to one's enemies or answering their insults
questions.D: winning every argument by being cleverer than one's opponent
questions.explanation: Mrs Dubose breaks her morphine addiction before dying.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In 'Wuthering Heights', the story is told mainly through
questions.A: Lockwood's diary and Nelly Dean's narration to him
questions.B: Heathcliff's letters to Catherine from abroad
questions.C: Catherine's diary alone, found after her death
questions.D: an omniscient narrator who comments on events
questions.explanation: Bronte uses a double frame narrative: Lockwood records what Nelly tells him.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: Heathcliff is brought to Wuthering Heights as a child by
questions.A: Mr Earnshaw, who found him in Liverpool
questions.B: Hindley, who bought him from gypsies
questions.explanation: Old Mr Earnshaw returns from Liverpool with the 'gypsy brat'.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: Catherine's declaration 'I am Heathcliff' in 'Wuthering Heights' expresses
questions.A: her sense that her identity is inseparable from his
questions.B: her plan to disguise herself as him
questions.C: her decision to marry him immediately
questions.explanation: She marries Edgar for status but feels her soul is one with Heathcliff's.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The two houses in 'Wuthering Heights' - the Heights and Thrushcross Grange - symbolise
questions.A: wild passion and civilised refinement respectively
questions.C: the town and the sea respectively
questions.explanation: The stormy Heights contrast with the calm, cultivated Grange.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: 'Wuthering Heights' ends with
questions.A: the union of Hareton Earnshaw and the younger Catherine
questions.B: the marriage of Heathcliff and Catherine
questions.C: the destruction of both houses by fire
questions.explanation: The second generation heals the feud after Heathcliff's death.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A novel such as 'To Kill a Mockingbird', which traces a child's growth in understanding of an adult world, can be described as
questions.explanation: The novel of formation follows the moral education of a young protagonist.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In 'To Kill a Mockingbird', the gifts left in the knothole of the oak tree come from
questions.explanation: Boo's secret gifts are ended when Nathan Radley fills the hole with cement.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In Osundare's 'Not My Business', the refrain 'What business of mine is it / So long they don't take the yam / From my savouring mouth?' expresses
questions.A: selfish indifference to the suffering of others
questions.B: courage in defending neighbours from the soldiers
questions.C: gratitude for a good harvest of yams and corn
questions.D: grief at the death of a friend taken by the jeep
questions.explanation: The speaker ignores each arrest until the jeep comes for him.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The ending of 'Not My Business', in which the jeep waits 'on my bewildered lawn', shows that
questions.A: silence in the face of injustice does not protect the silent
questions.B: the soldiers have come to reward the speaker
questions.C: the speaker has finally reported his neighbours
questions.explanation: The speaker who minded 'his business' becomes the next victim.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The characters Akanni, Danladi and Chinwe in 'Not My Business' represent
questions.A: ordinary Nigerians from different regions victimised by a repressive regime
questions.B: the speaker's children, who are taken away one after another by the soldiers
questions.C: the soldiers who carry out the arrests on the orders of the government
questions.D: traditional rulers of the three regions who collaborate with the regime
questions.explanation: Their names, drawn from different ethnic groups, show that oppression spares no one.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In Okara's 'Once Upon a Time', the father says that people once 'laughed with their hearts and their eyes' but now 'laugh with their teeth'. The contrast is between
questions.explanation: Genuine warmth has given way to hollow social pretence.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In 'Once Upon a Time', the father wants to 'unlearn all these muting things' and asks his son to
questions.A: show him how to laugh as he used to laugh as a child
questions.B: teach him to speak English like the people in town
questions.C: forgive him for leaving home to work in the city
questions.D: avoid all strangers who laugh with their teeth
questions.explanation: The child's natural laughter represents the innocence the father has lost.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: 'I have learned to wear many faces / like dresses' in 'Once Upon a Time' is an example of
questions.explanation: The speaker compares his changing false expressions to changes of clothing.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In Soyinka's 'Night', the night is presented as
questions.A: an oppressive female presence whose 'hand is heavy' on the speaker's brow
questions.B: a friendly companion who brings rest and sweet dreams to the tired speaker
questions.C: a soldier guarding the city against the thieves who come out after dark
questions.D: a child playing on the beach while the speaker watches from the shore
questions.explanation: The poem opens 'Your hand is heavy, Night, upon my brow' and personifies night as a powerful woman.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The line 'Hide me now, when night children haunt the earth' in Soyinka's 'Night' expresses the speaker's
questions.A: fear and desire for protection from the mysterious forces of night
questions.B: joy at the arrival of his children after a long journey home
questions.C: wish to join the night children in their games on the sand
questions.D: anger at the noise of the city that keeps him awake till dawn
questions.explanation: The speaker feels vulnerable to the 'misted calls' that could 'undo' him.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In Osundare's 'The Leader and the Led', the animals reject the lion, hyena, giraffe and others as leaders because
questions.A: each has a flaw that makes it unfit to rule alone
questions.B: they are all too old to lead the animals to water
questions.C: they refuse to be chosen and hide in the forest
questions.D: they cannot speak the language of the other animals
questions.explanation: The lion's 'paws are too fierce', the hyena's 'a stench', and so on.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The conclusion of 'The Leader and the Led' - a leader who 'knows how to follow' and followers 'mindful of their right to lead' - advocates
questions.A: leadership based on humility and mutual accountability
questions.B: military rule by the strongest and most feared animal
questions.C: the rule of the oldest animal in the whole forest
questions.D: the abolition of all leaders and the end of authority
questions.explanation: The forest sage recommends 'a hybrid of habits' - balanced, accountable leadership.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In Senghor's 'Black Woman', the poet celebrates the woman as
questions.A: a symbol of Africa's beauty and life-giving strength
questions.B: a victim of colonial exploitation and forced labour
questions.C: a rival to the European woman in elegance and wealth
questions.D: a warrior in battle against the invaders of her land
questions.explanation: 'Naked woman, black woman, clothed with your colour which is life' - the woman embodies Africa itself.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: 'Black Woman' ends with the poet's wish to 'fix' the woman's beauty in the Eternal 'before jealous fate turns you to ashes'. This expresses
questions.A: the desire to preserve beauty through art against time and death
questions.B: fear of the woman's anger if the poet should ever leave her
questions.C: regret at leaving Africa for a life of exile in France
questions.D: a prayer for children who will inherit the woman's beauty
questions.explanation: The poem, like many love poems, offers art as a defence against mortality.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The tone of Osundare's 'Not My Business' in the first three stanzas is best described as
questions.explanation: The speaker's callous refrain is ironic; the poet condemns what the speaker approves.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A common feature of 'Not My Business' and 'Once Upon a Time' is that both
questions.A: use a simple, conversational voice to criticise a social evil
questions.B: are written in strict sonnet form
questions.C: celebrate the beauty of the African landscape
questions.D: are addressed to a dead lover
questions.explanation: Both poems use plain language and a speaking voice to expose indifference and hypocrisy.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The image of the smile that is 'like a snake's bare fangs' in 'Once Upon a Time' suggests
questions.A: the speaker's awareness that his own false smile has become dangerous and unnatural
questions.B: his admiration for snakes, which he regards as the most beautiful of all creatures
questions.C: his fear of animals, which has grown since he moved from the village to the town
questions.D: his happiness at being home again among people who laugh with their hearts
questions.explanation: Looking in the mirror, the speaker sees that his social smile has become predatory.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: Byron's 'She Walks in Beauty' compares the woman to
questions.A: 'the night / Of cloudless climes and starry skies'
questions.B: 'a summer's day' that is 'more lovely and more temperate'
questions.C: 'a red, red rose / That's newly sprung in June'
questions.D: 'a host of golden daffodils' beside the lake
questions.explanation: The opening simile joins darkness and light in her beauty.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In 'She Walks in Beauty', 'One shade the more, one ray the less, / Had half impaired the nameless grace' suggests that the woman's beauty
questions.A: depends on a perfect balance of dark and light
questions.B: is entirely a matter of bright colours
questions.C: is spoilt by too much light
questions.explanation: Any change in the mixture would diminish her grace.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The closing lines of 'She Walks in Beauty' - 'A mind at peace with all below, / A heart whose love is innocent!' - show that the poem praises
questions.A: inner goodness as well as outward beauty
questions.explanation: The final stanza moves from appearance to moral character.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In Heaney's 'Digging', the pen is compared to
questions.A: a gun and then to a spade
questions.explanation: 'The squat pen rests; snug as a gun' opens the poem; it ends 'I'll dig with it'.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The speaker in 'Digging' says 'I've no spade to follow men like them' but resolves to dig with his pen. This expresses
questions.A: his continuation of the family tradition of labour through writing
questions.B: his rejection of his father and grandfather and their way of life
questions.C: his decision to give up poetry and become a farmer like them
questions.D: his shame at being a poet in a family of hard-working farmers
questions.explanation: Writing becomes the poet's own form of digging into the past and the soil of memory.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: 'The cold smell of potato mould, the squelch and slap / Of soggy peat' in 'Digging' appeals to the senses of
questions.explanation: The lines combine olfactory, auditory and tactile imagery, with onomatopoeia in 'squelch and slap'.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In Maya Angelou's 'Still I Rise', the repeated line 'I rise' functions as
questions.explanation: The refrain builds to a triumphant climax against oppression.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: 'You may write me down in history / With your bitter, twisted lies' in 'Still I Rise' addresses
questions.A: those who have oppressed and misrepresented black people
questions.B: the poet's own children, who have forgotten their history
questions.C: a lover who has left her for another woman
questions.D: a teacher at school who gave her low marks in history
questions.explanation: The 'you' is the oppressor whose version of history the speaker rejects.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: 'Cause I walk like I've got oil wells / Pumping in my living room' in 'Still I Rise' conveys
questions.A: confident self-worth that provokes the oppressor
questions.B: the speaker's actual wealth from the oil business
questions.C: the speaker's love of luxury and expensive things
questions.D: a complaint about poverty and the lack of a proper house
questions.explanation: The exaggerated image asserts pride and dignity that need no material basis.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: 'I'm a black ocean, leaping and wide' in 'Still I Rise' is
questions.A: a metaphor of vast, unstoppable power
questions.D: a description of the sea at night
questions.explanation: The speaker identifies herself with an ocean - immense and irresistible.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In W. W. Gibson's 'The Stone', the speaker is asked by a young woman to
questions.A: cut a gravestone for her lover, who was killed by a fall of stone
questions.B: build her a house of stone on the hill above the village
questions.C: carve a statue of the king for the square in the market town
questions.D: break the stone that blocks the road to her lover's farm
questions.explanation: The girl's lover died when 'the stone fell on him', and she asks the mason for 'a stone for him'.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The repeated question 'And will you cut a stone for him?' in Gibson's 'The Stone' gives the poem the quality of
questions.explanation: The refrain-like repetition and the tale of love and death are ballad features.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In Chaucer's 'The Nun's Priest's Tale', Chauntecleer is
questions.A: a proud cock who is nearly carried off by a fox
questions.D: a miller who cheats his customers
questions.explanation: The tale is a beast fable set in a poor widow's yard.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The fox in 'The Nun's Priest's Tale' captures Chauntecleer by
questions.A: flattering him into closing his eyes to crow
questions.B: digging under the fence at night
questions.explanation: Vanity makes Chauntecleer shut his eyes and stretch his neck to sing.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: Chauntecleer escapes from the fox by
questions.A: persuading the fox to open his mouth to taunt the pursuers
questions.B: pecking out the fox's eyes while he runs through the wood
questions.C: calling on Pertelote and the hens to attack the fox together
questions.D: promising the fox a fat hen if he will let him go free
questions.explanation: The tale's morals: beware flattery, and do not speak when you should keep silent.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: 'The Nun's Priest's Tale' is an example of
questions.explanation: Chaucer treats a farmyard incident in the grand manner of epic and romance.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In Fleur Adcock's 'The Telephone Call', the speaker is told that she has won a huge lottery prize, but the callers finally reveal that
questions.A: they do not deal in money and only wanted her to experience the feeling of winning
questions.B: she must pay a large registration fee before the prize money can be sent to her
questions.C: the prize has been given to someone else because she took too long to answer
questions.D: she has won a car instead of money and must collect it from another city
questions.explanation: The 'Universal Lotteries' turn out to be 'Experiential'; the call is a hoax.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The tone of the callers in 'The Telephone Call' is best described as
questions.explanation: Their chirpy patter contrasts with the emptiness of what they offer.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In Angelou's 'Caged Bird', the free bird that 'dares to claim the sky' is contrasted with the caged bird whose 'wings are clipped and his feet are tied'. The two birds represent
questions.A: the privileged and the oppressed in a divided society
questions.C: summer and winter in the American South
questions.D: the young and the old in one family
questions.explanation: The free bird enjoys unearned liberty while the caged bird, standing for the oppressed, can only sing of freedom.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: T. S. Eliot's 'The Journey of the Magi' ends with the speaker saying he 'should be glad of another death' because
questions.A: the birth of Christ has made his old world and beliefs meaningless
questions.B: the journey has exhausted him physically and he longs for rest
questions.C: he has lost his camels and gifts and cannot face his people
questions.D: he wishes to return to Bethlehem and die near the child
questions.explanation: The Birth was 'hard and bitter agony... like Death, our death'; he is alienated from 'the old dispensation'.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The image 'three trees on the low sky' in 'The Journey of the Magi' foreshadows
questions.explanation: The three trees anticipate the three crosses of Calvary.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: 'Digging' and 'Still I Rise' are alike in that both
questions.A: draw strength from ancestors or forebears
questions.B: are written in strict sonnet form
questions.D: mourn the death of a child
questions.explanation: Heaney honours his father and grandfather; Angelou speaks as 'the dream and the hope of the slave'.
